fact: 1914年8月4日，威尔逊总统发布中立公告，宣布美国对奥匈与塞尔维亚、德国与俄国、德国与法国之间的战争保持「严格与公正的中立」。公告同时明确：美国的法律与条约「不干涉意见与同情的自由表达，也不干涉军火与战争物资的商业制造或销售」，但禁止在美国境内征兵、装备交战方军舰与组织军事远征。

sources.title: World War I Document Archive（worldwar1.com）, August 1914: The United States Declares Neutrality（中立公告全文）
sources.quote: Whereas the laws and treaties of the United States, without interfering with the free expression of opinion and sympathy, or with the commercial manufacture or sale of arms or munitions of war, nevertheless impose upon all persons who may be within their territory and jurisdiction the duty of an impartial neutrality during the existence of the contest

sources.quote: NEUTRALITY OF IS PROCLAIMED By Associated Press Washington, D. C., Aug. 4. —The proclamation of neutrality of the United States in the European war, issued to-day by President Wilson, is aa follows: Whereas a state of war, unhap pily, exists between Austria- Hungary and Servla and between Germany and Russia and between Germany and France

fact: 1914年8月19日，威尔逊发表中立政策声明，要求美国人在「事实上与名义上」都保持中立，「在思想上如同在行动上一样不偏不倚」，并警告党派偏见是「最深层、最微妙、最本质的破坏中立」。这份声明针对的是国内德裔、爱尔兰裔与英裔移民之间迅速升温的站队情绪。

sources.title: World War I Document Archive（worldwar1.com）, Presidential Statement on American Neutrality, August 19, 1914
sources.quote: The effect of the war upon the United States will depend upon what American citizens say and do. ... The United States must be neutral in fact, as well as in name, during these days that are to try men’s souls. We must be impartial in thought, as well as action, must put a curb upon our sentiments, as well as upon every transaction that might be construed as a preference of one party to the struggle before another.

fact: 纽约证券交易所于1914年7月31日自愿关闭；11月28日部分重开，只交易债券并设最低价；12月12日恢复股票交易，仍限于限制性交易并设最低价；限制逐步放宽，1915年4月1日完全解除。停市期间，交易所后街出现场外「新街市场」，约35名经纪人以现金撮合，日成交量估计8000至42000股。

sources.title: FRASER, 美国司法部长办公室备忘录：United States Action in the Field of Foreign Exchange During the Great War（1939，收录于 Morgenthau Diaries Vol.206）
sources.quote: The New York Stock Exchange voluntarily closed on July 31,1914. ... On November 28, the exchange was partially opened for trading in bonds at fixed minimum prices. On December 12, 1914, trading in stocks was resumed on a restricted basis, subject also to minimum prices. These restrictions were gradually relaxed and were finally removed on April 1,1915.

sources.title: The New York Times, Along Wall Street, 1935-09-22（回顾1914年停市与场外市场）
sources.quote: Following the closing of the Stock Exchange, the narrow lane back of the Exchange became the scene of unofficial trading in securities. About thirty-five brokers gathered and handled a daily business variously estimated at from 8,000 to 42,000 shares. All dealings were for cash

fact: 1914年8月至10月，美国财政部依据《奥尔德里奇—弗里兰德法》向银行投放大量紧急货币，应对银行与个人提取、窖藏现金造成的挤兑；12个联邦储备银行于1914年11月16日正式开业，此后货币需求转由联储体系供给。

sources.title: FRASER, 美国司法部长办公室备忘录：United States Action in the Field of Foreign Exchange During the Great War
sources.quote: The Treasury made available to banks during August and October,1914, a large amount of emergency currency to take care of extraordinary demands for currency resulting from the withdrawal and hoarding of full money by banks and individuals. The Federal Reserve Banks opened on November 16, 1914, and currency requirements were subsequently furnished by such banks.

sources.title: FRASER, Federal Reserve Board Minutes, 1914-10-24
sources.quote: he had concluded to notify the several Federal Reserve banks that he would announce the establishment on the 16th day of November, 1914, of the Federal reserve bank in each of the twelve Federal reserve districts.

fact: 1914年9月21日，财政部长与联邦储备委员会批准设立1亿美元黄金基金，由银行与信托公司出资、纽约银行家委员会管理，用以稳定外汇市场；实际只动用约四分之一，运往国外的黄金不超过1000万美元。到1914年11月11日，美元不再贴水，纽约开始取代伦敦成为部分国家的融资市场。

sources.title: FRASER, 美国司法部长办公室备忘录：United States Action in the Field of Foreign Exchange During the Great War
sources.quote: The Secretary of the Treasury and Federal Reserve Board approved on September 21, 1914, a plan for setting up a gold fund of $100 millions the gold was contributed by banks and trust companies and the fund was administered by a committee of bankers in New York. ... Only a comparatively small percentage of the amount subscribed was actually called for (about 25 percent), and not more than $10,000,000 was actually exported

sources.title: Wikipedia, Financial crisis of 1914
sources.quote: On November 11, 1914, the dollar no longer traded at a discount, marking the day when the U.S. emerged as a financial leader. By January 1915, countries visited New York City, instead of London, to raise capital.

fact: 1914年纽约工会工时工资：砌砖工每小时0.75美元、每周44小时、周薪33美元；木匠每小时0.65美元、周薪28.73美元；油漆工每小时0.50美元、周薪22美元。同年6月纽约代表性工厂的平均周薪为12.70美元，10月降至12.26美元。

fact: 美国棉花约六成产量销往海外。1914年战争爆发后棉价崩溃、报价一度无法取得，南方各地出现每磅5美分甚至更低的零星成交；11月1日平均价6.8美分，上年同期为13美分，棉农全年损失约4.55亿美元，为1898年以来最低。10月24日联邦储备委员会批准设立1.35亿美元棉花贷款基金，按每磅6美分放贷。此后棉价回升：一年后12.5美分，两年后21美分。

sources.title: FRASER, Annual Report of the Federal Reserve Board, 1914（Cotton Loan Fund）
sources.quote: about 60 per cent of the total cotton, production of the United States is annually sent abroad ... Prices collapsed, quotations were unobtainable, and with the markets utterly demoralized, sales were made sporadically at various points in the South at 5 cents per pound—and even lower have been reported. ... The plan provided that to the $100,000,000 thus to be raised should be added a further sum of $35,000,000

sources.title: The New York Times, Cotton Syndicate Declared Legal, 1914-11-08
sources.quote: Wars effect on the price of cotton and cottonseed has caused a loss of about $455,000,000 to American cotton farmers this year ... Cotton prices on Nov. 1 averaged 6.8 cents a pound, while a year ago the price was 13 cents. This year’s prices are the lowest since 1898.

sources.title: The New York Times, Proposed Cotton Loan, 1933-09-28（回顾1914年棉花贷款基金与战后价格）
sources.quote: The banks then cooperated in raising a fund of $135,000,000, which they offered to lend the cotton farmers on the basis of 6 cents a pound. ... A year later cotton sold at 12½ cents; two years later at 21.

fact: 1914年8月4日中立公告列明禁止行为：接受交战方委任服役、应募为交战方士兵或水兵、招募他人越境应募、为交战方武装或装备船只、增强军舰武力、从美国领土发起军事远征。公告不禁止意见表达与私人贸易，但禁止美国水域被交战方用作作战基地；违者「自担风险」，得不到美国政府保护。

sources.title: The Frostburg Spirit, 1914-08-13（Chronicling America 影像 OCR，公告禁止行为清单）
sources.quote: the following acts are forbidden to be done, under severe penalties, within the territory and jurisdiction of the United States, to wit: 1— Accepting and exercising a commission to serve either of the said belligerents by land or by sea against the other belligerent. 2 Enlisting or entering into the service of either of the said belligerents as a soldier ... 8 — Fitting out and arming any ship to be employed in the service of the belligerents.
